catalog_quote: La palabra fonológica consta de dos a cinco sílabas en una unidad secuencial marcada por un núcleo. El núcleo es la sílaba que recibe mayor fuerza intensiva, un ligero alargamiento opcional de la vocal, y generalmente un tono ascendente (Headland 1976:18). El uw cuwa es una lengua no-tonal en que el acento prosódico tiene significado: wíquinro 'yo doy', wiquínro 'yo vengo', ába 'sangre' abá 'madre'. Para un hispano o anglohablante es difícil determinar el acento ya que el tono alto y el acento en uw cuwa no necesariamente van juntos en la misma sílaba como sí sucede en español e inglés. [p. 9] Las palabras se acentúan en la penúltima sílaba a menos que se indique en otro lugar. [Márquez et al. 1988, 'Signos y grafías'] (´) la tilde indica vocal tónica. Si una palabra no lleva tilde, se acentúa en la penúltima sílaba de derecha a izquierda.

new_statements.quote: La palabra fonológica consta de dos a cinco sílabas en una unidad secuencial marcada por un núcleo. El núcleo es la sílaba que recibe mayor fuerza intensiva, un ligero alargamiento opcional de la vocal, y generalmente un tono ascendente (Headland 1976:18). El uw cuwa es una lengua no-tonal en que el acento prosódico tiene significado: wíquinro 'yo doy', wiquínro 'yo vengo', ába 'sangre' abá 'madre'. [p. 9:] Las palabras se acentúan en la penúltima sílaba a menos que se indique en otro lugar.
new_statements.translation: The phonological word consists of two to five syllables in a sequential unit marked by a nucleus. The nucleus is the syllable that receives the greatest intensity, an optional slight lengthening of the vowel, and generally a rising tone (Headland 1976:18). Uw cuwa is a non-tonal language in which prosodic accent is meaningful: wíquinro 'I give', wiquínro 'I come', ába 'blood', abá 'mother'. [p. 9:] Words are stressed on the penultimate syllable unless indicated otherwise.
new_statements.citation: Headland, Edna R. (comp.). 1997. Diccionario bilingüe: Uw cuwa (Tunebo)-Español, Español-Uw cuwa (Tunebo) con una gramática uw cuwa (tuneba). Bogotá: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. pp. 16 (§1.1) and 9 (Introducción, 'La ortografía uw cuwa').
new_statements.locator: p. 16, §1.1 'Los fonemas' (final two paragraphs); p. 9 last sentence of 'La ortografía uw cuwa'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (3 pp., Rosetta Project scan of Headland 1997 pp. 15-17) and viewed the page render book p. 16, p. 2). The quoted passage is there verbatim, diacritics included: "La palabra fonológica consta de dos a cinco sílabas en una unidad secuencial marcada por un núcleo. El núcleo es la sílaba que recibe mayor fuerza intensiva, un ligero alargamiento opcional de la vocal, y generalmente un tono ascendente (Headland 1976:18).[fn 7] El uw cuwa es una lengua no-tonal en que el acento prosódico tiene significado: wíquinro 'yo doy', wiquínro 'yo vengo', ába 'sangre' abá 'madre'. Para un hispano o anglohablante es difícil determinar el acento ya que el tono alto y el acento en uw cuwa no necesariam…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Each phonological word (2-5 syllables) has one stressed nucleus (intensity, optional lengthening, usually rising pitch). Stress is contrastive/lexical, with minimal pairs on both bisyllables and trisyllables; the orthographic default is penultimate stress, with a written tilde for anything else, so the pattern is a penult default with lexically specified exceptions (final and antepenultimate stress attested).
new_statements.exceptions: Non-penult stress must be marked orthographically ('a menos que se indique en otro lugar'); minimal pairs show antepenult vs penult (wíquinro/wiquínro) and penult vs final (ába/abá). Headland adds (p. 16) that high tone and stress do not necessarily fall on the same syllable, unlike Spanish/English (Janet Barnes, p.c.), and that Tegría and Cobaría speakers differ in some segmental variants.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('palabra fonológica'); the same page gives a single sentence-level intonation pattern (final fall on all phrases, including questions). Dialects covered: Cobaría and Tegría (both Central Tunebo). Márquez et al. 1988 (Cobaría) use the same convention: unmarked words are stressed on the penult, tilde marks the stressed vowel otherwise.
new_statements.identity_note: Headland 1997 describes Uw Cuwa of the Cobaría and Tegría communities (both Central Tunebo, cent2150) and notes segmental preferences by community; Márquez et al. 1988 is explicitly the Cobaría dialect. No separate glottocode applies.

new_statements.quote: p. 16: "La palabra fonológica consta de dos a cinco sílabas en una unidad secuencial marcada por un núcleo. El núcleo es la sílaba que recibe mayor fuerza intensiva, un ligero alargamiento opcional de la vocal, y generalmente un tono ascendente (Headland 1976:18). El uw cuwa es una lengua no-tonal en que el acento prosódico tiene significado: wíquinro 'yo doy', wiquínro 'yo vengo', ába 'sangre' abá 'madre'. Para un hispano o anglohablante es difícil determinar el acento ya que el tono alto y el acento en uw cuwa no necesariamente van juntos en la misma sílaba como sí sucede en español e inglés." p. 9: "Las palabras se acentúan en la penúltima sílaba a menos que se indique en otro lugar."
new_statements.translation: p. 16: "The phonological word consists of two to five syllables in a sequential unit marked by a nucleus. The nucleus is the syllable that receives the greatest intensity, an optional slight lengthening of the vowel, and generally a rising tone (Headland 1976:18). Uw cuwa is a non-tonal language in which prosodic stress is meaningful: wíquinro 'I give', wiquínro 'I come', ába 'blood', abá 'mother'. For a Spanish or English speaker it is hard to determine the stress, since high tone and stress in uw cuwa do not necessarily go together on the same syllable as they do in Spanish and English." p. 9: "Words are stressed on the penultimate syllable unless indicated otherwise."

Verified on the page scan: printed p. 16, header 'DICCIONARIO BILINGÜE UW CUWA-ESPAÑOL, ESPAÑOL-UW CUWA') carries the two quoted paragraphs verbatim, diacritics intact: 'La palabra fonológica consta de dos a cinco sílabas en una unidad secuencial marcada por un núcleo. El núcleo es la sílaba que recibe mayor fuerza intensiva, un ligero alargamiento opcional de la vocal, y generalmente un tono ascendente (Headland 1976:18).' then 'El uw cuwa es una lengua no-tonal en que el acento prosódico tiene significado: wíquinro 'yo doy', wiquínro 'yo vengo', ába 'sangre' abá 'madre'. Para un hispano o anglohablante es difícil determinar el acento ya que el tono alto y el acento en uw cu…
new_statements.relation_note: Same source and same passages as the existing statement (p. 16 and p. 9); The p. 9 penult-default sentence refines the p. 16 contrastive statement (penult is the unmarked position; stress elsewhere is lexical and written with the acute). The catalog record for cent2150 has an empty rule field; the reading 'lexical (unpredictable), penult default' is what this work supports.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is contrastive and lexically fixed: each phonological word (2-5 syllables) has one nucleus syllable marked by greater intensity, optional slight vowel lengthening and usually a rising tone, and minimal pairs differ by its position (wíquinro/wiquínro, ába/abá). The dictionary's orthography treats the penult as the unmarked default and marks stress with an acute only where it falls elsewhere. The language is explicitly non-tonal; high pitch and stress need not coincide.
new_statements.exceptions: Penultimate is only an orthographic default ('a menos que se indique en otro lugar'); words with final or antepenultimate stress (abá 'madre', wíquinro 'yo doy') are marked with the acute. Footnote 8 credits the remark on tone vs stress to phonetician Janet Barnes (p.c.). Intonation (§1.2): a single falling pattern at the end of all phrases, questions included.
new_statements.identity_note: Headland 1997 describes the Cobaría and Tegría varieties of Uw Cuwa (its footnotes 9-11 on pp. 16-17 note Tegría vs Cobaría preferences); Márquez et al. 1988 describes Cobaría. Glottolog lists Cobaría, Tegría, U'w Cuwa and U'wa as alternate names of cent2150, so both belong to this languoid. Rochereau 1926-27 covers 'la lengua tuneba y sus dialectos' but was not opened, so which dialects it treats is unverified.

new_statements.quote: p. 18 §1: «La palabra fonológica consta de dos a cinco sílabas en una unidad de ritmo marcada por un núcleo. El núcleo es la sílaba que recibe fuerza balística, un ligero alargamiento opcional de la vocal, y generalmente un tono ascendente.» pp. 24 §4: «El acento es contrastivo dentro de las palabras y se caracteriza por la intensidad, por el alargamiento fonético opcional del núcleo de la sílaba acentuada, y por los fenómenos tonales. /wíkinro/ 'yo doy' /ába/ 'sangre' /wikínro/ 'yo vengo' /abá/ 'madre' ... /káka/ 'boca' /kaká/ 'abuela' ... /batamá/ 'tipo de culebra' /anará/ 'cabello'»
new_statements.translation: p. 18: 'The phonological word consists of two to five syllables in a rhythm unit marked by a nucleus. The nucleus is the syllable that receives ballistic force, a slight optional lengthening of the vowel, and generally a rising tone.' p. 24: 'Stress is contrastive within words and is characterized by intensity, by optional phonetic lengthening of the nucleus of the stressed syllable, and by tonal phenomena. /wíkinro/ 'I give' /ába/ 'blood' /wikínro/ 'I come' /abá/ 'mother' ... /káka/ 'mouth' /kaká/ 'grandmother' ... /batamá/ 'kind of snake' /anará/ 'hair''.
new_statements.citation: Headland, Paul & Edna Headland. 1976. Fonología del tunebo. In: Sistemas fonológicos de idiomas colombianos 3, 17-26. Lomalinda: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
new_statements.locator: p. 18 §1 'La palabra fonológica'; pp. 24-25 §4 'El fonema suprasegmental'; p. 26 §8 'Ortografía' (pp. 12, 18-19, 20)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened 20 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the Title 'Sistemas fonológicos de idiomas colombianos 3', Author 'Headland, Paul and Edna Headland', keywords 15902 tuf) and its scanned; rendered pp. 12, 18, 19, 20 (= printed 18, 24, 25, 26) at 150 dpi and read the images. p. 18 §1 'La palabra fonológica' reads exactly 'La palabra fonológica consta de dos a cinco sílabas en una unidad de ritmo marcada por un núcleo. El núcleo es la sílaba que recibe fuerza balística, un ligero alargamiento opcional de la vocal, y generalmente un tono ascendente. (Vea la sección 4, para la excepción a la última característica.)' with examples /káyina/, /kumorokʷáno/, /werháykʷano/, /óka/, /átkara/. p. 24 §4 'El fone…
new_statements.relation_note: This is the primary phonology that Headland 1997:16 cites ('Headland 1976:18') for the existing catalog statement; it states the same contrastive (lexical) stress with the same minimal pairs, and adds detail the 1997 summary lacks: the phonological-word domain (2-5 syllables, one nucleus), the tonal realization of stress (high/rising) and the marginal falling-tone (or length) contrast on some initial-stressed disyllables, plus the spelling rule that only non-penult stress is. Dialect described: Cobaría (fieldwork 1964-65, data to 1975). Live SIL file is still not reachable by automated download on two attempts; the copy read is the Internet Archive copy (2010-07-14) of the old SIL Colombia…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Cobaría Tunebo has one stress (the 'nucleus') per phonological word of 2-5 syllables; its position is lexically contrastive and not predictable (minimal pairs wíkinro/wikínro, ába/abá, káka/kaká; examples with initial, medial, penult and final stress: káyina, kumorokwáno, werháykwano, óka, átkara, báyara, bahíta, batamá, anará). Stress is realized as intensity, optional lengthening and pitch: normally high tone (rising in slow speech), marked /´/. A second, falling tone (marked with a grave accent) occurs on the stressed syllable of some disyllables stressed on the first syllable and contrasts with the high tone there (ása 'yo' vs àsa 'coca', áka 'piedra' vs àka 'cara', rúka 'primo' vs rùka 'olla de barro'); the authors note the falling-tone nucleus is often longer, so it could alternatively be analysed as vowel length. The language is otherwise described with stress ('acento') as its only suprasegmental phoneme, not as tonal. Orthography (p. 26): the accent is written only when stress does not fall on the penultimate syllable (and coincides with high tone), i.e. penult is treated as the unmarked default in spelling.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described: each phonological word (2-5 syllables) has a single nucleus; no secondary stress is mentioned.
new_statements.exceptions: Falling tone [grave] instead of high/rising tone on the stressed first syllable of some disyllables (possible reanalysis as vowel length); epenthetic unstressed /i/ breaking consonant clusters adds a syllable without moving stress (íbta ~ íbita 'camino', kánta ~ kánita); orthographic convention leaves penult stress unmarked.
new_statements.identity_note: Headland & Headland 1976 explicitly describes the Cobaría dialect (of three named dialects: Cobaría, Barro Negro, Agua Blanca), fieldwork in Cobaría, Boyacá, 1964-65 with data to 1975; Headland & Levinsohn 1977 uses the same Cobaría consultants (Sarare region). Cobaría is a Glottolog alternate name of cent2150 Central Tunebo, so both are about this language. Constenla 1981 cites 'Tunebo' only as a secondary comparandum (variety unspecified in the abstract).
